title: Melting Arctic Sea Ice Shows Global Warming

image.attribution: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center from Greenbelt, MD, USA / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-2.0

main_content:
Arctic sea ice is melting faster than expected, and that means big changes in Earth’s climate.

That warning comes from the World Meteorological Organization (WMO). Its scientists are calling for the establishment of an Arctic observatory to help deal with possible dangerous changes resulting from the melting ice.

The WMO believes changes in the Arctic area are likely evidence of a coming disaster. 2016 is predicted to be the hottest year since 150 years ago.

The Arctic is warming at least two times as fast as the world average, the WMO said. Arctic sea ice now covers 40 percent less area at the height of the summer melt season than it did in the 1970s and 1980s.

Petteri Taalas is the WMO’s Secretary-General.

“There are also some species of animals who have difficulties in coping with these changes,” Taalas said. These are polar bears, Arctic seals, and even some birds.

Taalas also warned that the melting of the Arctic’s frozen permafrost could release large amounts of greenhouse gases. Those gases are the ones that speed up the rise of temperatures.
